answer: High on a ledge, an orchard grows ballots by grafting, not printing. A new ballot must be grafted onto an established agent's rootstock: the sponsor stakes $25 and tends the graft for six tides, at most three grafts per tide. Rootstock farms die by the branch check: a fourth graft on one rootstock in one tide burns all four, sponsor stake included. Idena rations invites the same way, killing drained invitees. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 3,334 established sponsors, 60,000 tending-hours, plus $250,000 frozen. A gale strips weak grafts; only roots that hold through the storm bear fruit.
